Given the has cold winters, the standalone baseline system could not provide the nominal 14.1 kW of heating capacity, and backup heating (COP ≤ 1) is required. The simulated HP-TES can provide heating capacity of 15 – 17 kW during peak periods without the need for auxiliary heating, resulting in peak demand reductions of up to 46% during the coldest winter months (Figure 45). During the summer, demand reductions did not exceed 11%, given the already near-PCM ambient conditions during peak hours.
